question: How does web search differ from classical IR, and how are web index size and duplicate pages estimated or handled?
contributions: Background on web history, graph structure, spam, advertising and user needs (19.1-19.4)
Capture-recapture index-size estimation with sampling biases (19.5)
Near-duplicate detection by shingling and min-hash sketches (19.6)

limits: 2008-9 web: AltaVista, Goto/Overture, Yahoo taxonomy, sponsored results shown 'to the right' of results; all dated.
No experiments; numbers (40% duplicates, in-degree 8-15, 2-3 keywords, k=4, 200 permutations, 0.9 threshold) are cited ranges or 'say' examples without data tables.
Threshold 0.9 and 80% are illustrations not tuned values.
Shingling treats a document as a set of exact term sequences: no semantic near-duplicates (paraphrase, translation, embeddings), no chunk-level dedup for RAG corpora.
Capture-recapture assumes independent uniform subsets, which the chapter itself says is far from true.
Chapter says the 200-permutation choice is 'suggested in the literature' but does not state error bounds.
practices: Remove exact duplicates first with a 64-bit fingerprint, then detect near duplicates with shingles (19.6, p.437-441).
Drop common HTML tags and integers before shingling so ubiquitous shingles do not mask duplication signal (p.440).
Use k=4 term shingles and a 200-permutation min-hash sketch, cluster with union-find, and prune pairs with super-shingles (p.438-441).
Do not pick random terms from a standard dictionary to sample a search index; build a sample web dictionary, and expect bias toward longer documents (p.436).
Measure navigational queries by precision at 1 and informational queries by comprehensiveness (p.432-433).

terms.definition: Given a positive integer k and a sequence of terms in a document d, define the k-shingles of d to be the set of all consecutive sequences of k terms in d.
The set of the 200 resulting values of x_i^pi (the smallest permuted hash under each of 200 random permutations) is the sketch psi(d_i) of d_i.
Shingles of the sorted sketch sequence; documents sharing one get a precise sketch-overlap computation.
Classical estimation technique: x|E1| ~ y|E2|, so |E1|/|E2| ~ y/x.
The manipulation of web page content for the purpose of appearing high up in search results for selected keywords.
The spammer's web server returns different pages depending on whether the http request comes from a crawler or a human browser.
Broder's three categories of web query: broad-topic information, a single entity's home page, or a prelude to a web transaction.
Web graph with IN, SCC and OUT sets plus tubes and tendrils.
Pricing model where an ad is priced by number of clicks rather than impressions.
